findings.message: AI review of revision 8. It is NOT the human literacy review the publication policy requires. literacy.review.status stays "pending" in the story file (I did not change it) and a qualified human must still review. 'pass' here only means I found no blocker or major finding. Automated checks cannot judge: spelling patterns are matched, not sound; syllable counts are estimates from vowel groups; readability figures are estimates and say nothing about how a particular child will read the text; the analyzer does not judge vocabulary, clue clarity, definition quality, whether a learning tag is real practice, or story quality. Sentence lengths I quote are my own hand counts, not analyzer output. I did not run the app, listen to the read-aloud voice, or test with a child; app behaviour is not judged here (read-aloud and the visible 'Optional' label belong to the app engineer).

REPORT FIGURES (taken from reports/literacy.r8.md and validation.r8.json): word sets sh-words 20/10, ch-words 23/8, th-words 16/8; every word used; each set on the shortest route to all three endings (ending-beam, ending-help, ending-dock); word-set-concepts-match-spelling: no mismatches; target concepts present (closed-syllable 404, digraph-sh 42, digraph-ch 24, digraph-th 165 matches); sentence-length: 0 sentences over 20 words; readability 714 words, average sentence 7.8 words, longest passage ending-help at 100 words, no words estimated at 4+ syllables; 18 glossary words with a definition; tagged moments comprehension 2, inference 3, sequencing 1, vocabulary 1, detail 2, engagement 1; validation: schema ok, graph ok, 3 of 3 endings reachable, state search complete (55 states). No word-set minimum is missed, no target pattern is absent, no word-set word fails its declared pattern (by spelling).

R7 MINOR 1 (window and Pip's place) - FIXED. Window: threshold still says "A gust of wind came in through the open window." then "Fen shut the window."; ending-help no longer mentions a window (paragraph 1 now reads "Fen called, and Pip flew down to the bench to tap Gran Tull's arm."), so the story agrees. Pip's place: ending-help paragraph 1 opens "Pip had hopped up the stairs behind Fen.", so Pip is in the lamp room before she "flew down to the bench", and paragraph 2 brings her back up ("She and Pip climbed the stairs, one slow step at a time."). Gran Tull's "Gran Tull heard from the bench" problem stays gone. Small leftovers, not findings: "had hopped" is past perfect, a tense a shaky reader may find slightly harder, and the text does not say why Pip was not mentioned in threshold or climax. Neither blocks understanding.

R7 MINOR 1b (long sentence) - FIXED. "She climbed the stairs, one slow step at a time, with Pip on her arm." is replaced by "She and Pip climbed the stairs, one slow step at a time." (12 words by my count; revision-notes.r8.md says 11). Paragraph 2 is now "Gran Tull looked up." / that sentence / "Then she put a hand on the chain." (4, 12, 8 words). The longest sentences I can find anywhere are about 14 to 15 words (start "Gran Tull, the old lamp keeper, sat on the bench by the tower door."; ending-dock "Next time, Fen would look at the mirror first, and ask for help."), under the brief's limit of 16 by hand count. ending-help is still the longest passage (100 words per the report, one more than in r7), so the length rests on five short paragraphs, not on long sentences. Acceptable.

R7 MINOR 4 (typing prompt wording) - FIXED for the story text. threshold puzzle prompt now reads "Type the word for the cold string in the dish. It is in the story you just read."; 'above' is gone and nothing points at the layout. The word 'wick' is in the passage ("The wick sat cold in its dish."), the hint ("It has four letters. It starts with w.") is unchanged and fair. The other half of the r7 finding (a visible 'Optional' label and whether read-aloud covers the prompt) is app behaviour, not story text, and stays with the app engineer; I did not check it in this review. Left open for them, not for the narrative designer.

R7 MINOR 2 (bench-clue inference tag) - PARTLY FIXED. Fixed: bench now carries learningTargets ["inference"]. The text supports it: "\"Look at the mirror, not the flame.\"" followed by "Fen did not know what she meant." leaves the reader a real 'why?' to wonder about before bench-clue answers it. Still open: bench-clue keeps ["inference", "comprehension"] (revision-notes.r8.md says this was left on purpose). Every link in that passage is stated in words ("Fog is wet air" / "It leaves wet mist on the brass mirror" / "A misty mirror makes the light dim"), so the inference tag on bench-clue is still thin; the comprehension tag is real. This is a tagging accuracy point and does not affect reading. The report's inference count (3) now includes both bench and bench-clue; the honest count of real inference moments is two (threshold and bench). Not a reason to withhold a pass.

R7 MINOR 3 (climax comprehension tag 'acceptable but light') - OPEN, UNCHANGED, and no change was requested. Text checked: "The mist wiped away, and the brass shone." then "The mirror caught the flame. A bright beam shot out into the thick fog." carries out the bench-clue explanation. The choice "Fen could pull it alone, or call Gran Tull." is about help, not about working something out. I still would not add tags to climax. Listed here only so the four r7 minors are all accounted for.

Locked-choice hint and routes, rechecked in story.r8.json. lockedHint "You need a cloth from the shed chest, and matches and a clue from Gran Tull." matches a pattern for exactly 76 characters once (limit 90), names all three requirements (soft-cloth, match-tin, damp-mirror) and where each comes from, and gives nothing away. The choice 'Wipe the mirror and light the wick' stays visible with the hint; 'Run down to the dock and wave' and 'Go back down the stairs to look for help' are never locked, so the child cannot get stuck. gathering offers the shed, the bench and the stairs, so every missing piece is reachable by going back.

OPTIONAL TYPING 'name-the-wick' (threshold) - NEVER BLOCKS A ROUTE, from the data. The puzzle in story.r8.json has no effects; no choice requires a puzzle (wipe-mirror requires only soft-cloth, match-tin and clue damp-mirror); validation.r8.json reports 3 of 3 endings reachable with the state search complete. Answers "wick" and "wicks" are accepted. It copies a word already in the passage (a ck word), so it is low pressure. Report: typing-balance ok, 1 puzzle in 8 non-ending passages.

READABILITY for ages 10 to 13 with dyslexia (an estimate, from the report figures and a full read of all 11 passages). Sentences are short, paragraphs are one to three sentences, each passage says who, where and what happened, dialogue uses quotation marks and 'said', and the harder words (wick, brass, beam, gust, stairs, knees, steady, fluttered, harbour, matches, window, mirror) have glossary help. The cause chain fog, mist, dim lamp, wipe is given in plain steps in bench-clue. The r8 changes made the story clearer, not harder: no new vocabulary was added, and the window and Pip's route now read without a contradiction. Tone is a gentle seaside mystery with no cruelty or injury. I find the text acceptable for the age range, pending the human review. Possible mispronunciations by a voice ('Tull', British 'harbour') are untested. The premise in metadata ("before the fishing boats come home") is a mild deadline that the reader never sees as a countdown; unchanged since earlier reviews and left for the human reviewer.

APP SETTINGS, story text only. NO MEANING THROUGH LAYOUT: no lists, tables, bold, colour words, 'on the left' or 'see below' in any passage, and the one layout pointer in the puzzle prompt is gone, so this now passes. READ-ALOUD: the meaning is in the paragraph words (sounds are written as words, e.g. start "tap, tap, tap"; gathering "a ship horn gave a low, sad call"); the voice and whether it reads the puzzle prompt are for the app engineer. OPTIONAL WORD HELP: the 18 glossary entries are keyed to words in the paragraphs and each hard word is also clear from context; choice labels and locked hints carry no glossary words that the plot depends on. NO TIME OR SPEED: no timer and no choice or hint mentions hurry; "twice as fast" (ending-help) is a result, not a choice. OPTIONAL TYPING THAT NEVER BLOCKS: see the typing note above. FAIR LOCKED-CHOICE HINT: 76 of 90 characters, fair (see above).
